tasks.short: Develop pricing strategies that balance margin, demand and customer satisfaction.

steps.what: Export realised prices, discounts, volumes and product costs.
Review competitor evidence and customer feedback for pricing constraints.

loop.input: Dated competitor evidence and approved customer feedback.
loop.output: Draft evidence brief separating observed prices, customer statements and hypotheses.
loop.check: Require source passages, comparable units and dates; the analyst checks ambiguous comparisons.
loop.stop: One pass and one repair per evidence batch; unsupported comparisons remain unresolved.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text feedback and differently packaged offers need contextual interpretation.

steps.what: Calculate margin, volume and customer-impact scenarios for alternative prices.
Agree positioning, acceptable tradeoffs and a proposed pricing strategy with sales and finance.
Write the pricing proposal and discount matrix.
Approve prices, discount limits and the effective date.
Enter approved prices and discount limits, checking dates and scope.

tasks.design: Use the {ERP} pricing controls and a deterministic scenario calculator on the {DATA_PLATFORM}, with explicit demand assumptions and margin floors. A bounded loop summarises source-linked evidence from the {DOCS}; the manager chooses the strategy and a template generator assembles the proposal. The {WORKFLOW} records commercial approval, then the pricing administrator checks the exact changes before release to the {ERP}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Comparable market evidence was difficult to assemble, and scenario workbooks were disconnected from approved price rules. Strategic uncertainty could not be solved by adding formulas.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing price controls handle limits and dates. AI-assisted coding makes a reusable calculator and approval connection cheaper, while a bounded model helps read mixed evidence.
tasks.still_hard: Demand responses are uncertain, competitors change offers, and customers may interpret the same increase differently. Historical sales alone do not establish price elasticity.
tasks.human_edge: Choose market positioning and judge which margin, fairness and relationship tradeoffs customers will accept.

ambition.what: Monthly segment pricing review triggered by margin or conversion changes.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends more time designing and evaluating pricing tests. They can recommend bounded experiments, while approval of price policy stays with the commercial director.

reach.task: Evaluate a limited price test on a defined product category.
reach.learn: Test design, conversion measurement, returns and customer communication.

evidence.claim: Price lists, discount matrices and approval thresholds can be implemented with deterministic rules.
Scenario calculations can expose assumptions but cannot establish causal demand responses from sales history alone.
Build ranges and review-time estimates require validation against the existing pricing configuration.

assumptions: The first release covers one price book and aggregate customer segments.
The scope excludes individual automated price discrimination.
Pricing recommendations use explicit demand assumptions rather than invented elasticity estimates.
Existing approval features are configured before custom release code is considered.
Employee performance scoring is outside scope.
unknowns: Whether realised prices include rebates, returns and retrospective discounts.
Which price rules the existing {ERP} supports.
Which contracts constrain price changes.
Who owns price approval and release checks.
Which data access and consultation requirements apply under national rules.
research_questions: Can existing price-book configuration support the required approval and rollback process?
Which product category permits a useful pricing test with limited customer disruption?
new_work: Maintain cost definitions, margin floors and demand assumptions.
Review evidence comparisons and stale competitor information.
Check release differences and effective dates.
Measure test outcomes and investigate unexpected customer responses.
tasks.statement: Develop pricing strategies, balancing firm objectives and customer satisfaction.

tasks.short: Develop and evaluate marketing strategy against objectives, market conditions and unit economics.

steps.what: Review business objectives, current performance and product economics.
Assess customer needs, market characteristics and competitor positions.

loop.input: Selected research, source-linked market signals and permitted customer feedback.
loop.output: Draft market assessment separating evidence, interpretations and gaps.
loop.check: Trace factual statements to dated sources; flag conflicting findings and unsupported segment claims.
loop.stop: One synthesis and one repair pass; unresolved interpretations go to the marketing manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Research uses varied language and contains competing interpretations that require contextual synthesis.

steps.what: Write strategic options covering target customers, positioning and channels.

loop.input: Strategy baseline, reviewed market assessment and a fixed option-comparison template.
loop.output: Draft strategy options with assumptions, trade-offs and evidence gaps.
loop.check: Require traceable factual claims, explicit assumptions and distinct choices; reject invented market sizes.
loop.stop: At most three options and one revision; the manager supplies missing evidence or rewrites weak choices.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates organise options, but expressing positioning choices and trade-offs needs contextual writing.

steps.what: Compare option economics, capacity needs and downside scenarios.
Debate strategic trade-offs with sales, finance and product leaders.
Approve target markets, positioning and resource commitments.
Record measures, owners and review dates for the approved strategy.

tasks.design: A strategy workspace combines approved figures from {BI} and {ERP} with source-linked research in {DOCS}. Bounded drafting steps prepare assessments and options, while deterministic calculations compare economics and downside assumptions. The marketing director approves the strategy decision, which creates review dates and measures in {PROJECT} and feeds campaign planning.
tasks.previous_blocker: Research, financial assumptions and strategy documents were disconnected. Polished presentations often hid which claims were evidence and which were judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable evidence templates and calculation modules can now be assembled with less coding effort. Bounded models can organise prose and draft alternatives, with source checks and explicit gaps.
tasks.still_hard: Positioning, willingness to pay and competitor response cannot be validated by document checks alone. Attractive narratives can still rest on weak evidence.
tasks.human_edge: Choose what to prioritise and what to abandon, judge customer relevance and build commitment across commercial teams.

ambition.what: Monthly review of the strategy's most fragile demand assumption.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends more time testing strategic assumptions with customers and less time assembling presentations. They gain a repeatable way to propose evidence-backed tests; final strategy and resource approval remain with the existing decision makers.

reach.task: Turn a positioning hypothesis into a measurable channel experiment.
reach.learn: Search intent, experimental design and the limits of attributed conversions.

evidence.claim: Campaign planning and branded drafting capabilities exist, supporting preparation rather than autonomous strategy approval.
Automated marketing reporting can provide the numerical baseline for strategy comparisons.
A vendor segmentation case reports improved revenue per email, but does not establish that strategy selection can be automated.
Strategic option quality requires market tests and human judgement beyond factual source checks.

assumptions: Research and financial evidence can be stored with source dates and access restrictions.
The target is strategy preparation and evaluation, with human approval of commitments.
Build ranges reuse forecast and campaign data components where available.
Access time includes research permissions, GDPR checks for customer feedback and national employee consultation where applicable.
unknowns: Which strategic decisions the marketing manager may make independently.
Whether product-level margins and usable customer research exist.
Which research licences permit automated processing.
How strategy success and review triggers are currently defined.
research_questions: Do source-linked drafts expose uncertainty clearly enough for decision makers?
Which low-cost market test can distinguish the leading strategic options?
How sensitive are option rankings to uncertain margin and demand assumptions?
new_work: Review evidence links and distinguish findings from interpretations.
Maintain comparison templates and financial assumptions.
Record rejected options and reasons for later review.
Design market tests and update strategy measures.
tasks.statement: Identify, develop, or evaluate marketing strategy, based on knowledge of establishment objectives, market characteristics, and cost and markup factors.

tasks.short: Evaluate product development costs, funding needs and financial returns.

steps.what: Read the product brief and assemble investment assumptions.

loop.input: Product brief and narrative investment assumptions.
loop.output: Draft assumption register with source passages and missing fields.
loop.check: Validate units and required fields; the manager checks meaning and unsupported assumptions.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair per brief; unresolved fields return to the author.
loop.why_not_simpler: Narrative briefs express assumptions inconsistently. Structured fields should bypass the loop.

steps.what: Export development budgets, commitments and actual expenditure.
Reconcile expenditure and allocate shared costs in the financial workbook.
Calculate profit, cash flow and return scenarios.
Challenge assumptions with product and finance colleagues and choose a funding recommendation.
Approve, defer or reject the proposed funding.

tasks.design: Configure scheduled extracts from the {ERP}, then use deterministic reconciliation and scenario calculations on the {DATA_PLATFORM}. A bounded extraction loop turns narrative briefs from the {DOCS} into draft assumptions, while a template generator produces traceable investment scenarios. Product discussions remain human, and the finance director approves funding through the {WORKFLOW}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Project codes, shared costs and narrative assumptions needed manual reconciliation. Existing financial models were feasible but costly to maintain across changing inputs.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of building mappings, validation and document templates. Existing exports and ordinary financial formulas provide most of the solution.
tasks.still_hard: Demand uncertainty, shared-cost allocation and the value of delaying investment remain judgement calls. Reliable calculations cannot make weak assumptions reliable.
tasks.human_edge: Challenge optimistic forecasts, weigh strategic options and accept responsibility for capital allocation.

ambition.what: Monthly product investment checkpoint using refreshed costs and downside scenarios.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time repairing financial workbooks and more time testing investment assumptions. They can propose staged funding checkpoints; formal spending authority remains with the budget holder.

reach.task: Design demand evidence for the most uncertain investment assumption.
reach.learn: Sampling limits, willingness-to-pay research and how uncertainty enters financial scenarios.

evidence.claim: Funnel provides marketing data connectors and reporting; this supports the integration pattern, not product investment modelling.
Cost reconciliation, scenario calculations and approval routing can use deterministic rules.
Build ranges and remaining-time estimates are planning hypotheses, not measured results.

assumptions: The first release covers one product portfolio and one finance entity.
Budget and expenditure records have usable project identifiers.
Unmapped costs are flagged rather than silently allocated.
Structured assumptions bypass the extraction loop.
The scope excludes employee monitoring; consultation under national rules is assessed if that changes.
unknowns: Which cost allocation rules finance accepts.
Whether commitments and actual expenditure can be exported together.
Who can approve each funding amount.
Whether an existing governed financial model already covers these scenarios.
Which access and consultation procedures apply.
research_questions: Does a standard investment template cover the portfolio without custom calculations?
Which historical decisions would change under realistic downside assumptions?
new_work: Review extracted assumptions and resolve missing inputs.
Maintain project mappings and cost allocation rules.
Investigate reconciliation exceptions.
Validate formulas when finance policy changes.
tasks.statement: Evaluate the financial aspects of product development, such as budgets, expenditures, research and development appropriations, or return-on-investment and profit-loss projections.

tasks.short: Lead marketing staff through hiring, training, daily direction and performance evaluation.

steps.what: Review workload, vacancies, planned absence and team skills.
Agree hiring needs and training priorities with the relevant budget owner.
Review recruiter shortlists against the agreed role criteria.
Interview candidates and discuss evidence with the hiring panel.
Approve the hiring decision and proposed offer terms.
Assign approved courses and track enrolment.
Allocate daily work and resolve competing demands.
Gather agreed goals, work examples and employee submissions for reviews.
Discuss performance, wellbeing and development with each employee.
Record the evaluation and agreed development actions.
Send reminders and check outstanding development actions.

tasks.design: Configure restricted views across {PROJECT}, {HCM}, {LMS} and {TALENT} to show workload, approved training and submitted review evidence. Existing workflows in {ATS}, {LMS} and {TALENT} handle approvals, enrolments, structured records and reminders. People select candidates, conduct interviews, allocate work and write evaluations; the design uses no model-based employee scoring.
tasks.previous_blocker: Personnel records were separated from delivery information, while access restrictions discouraged ad hoc integration. Administrative preparation was often treated as inseparable from sensitive management decisions.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing personnel systems can provide forms, permissions, evidence packs and reminders without model judgement. Small integrations and structured templates are cheaper to implement with AI-assisted coding.
tasks.still_hard: Trust, fair evaluation and difficult conversations remain demanding. Access boundaries, GDPR obligations and employee consultation under national rules can dominate rollout time.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise context behind results, give candid feedback, assess candidates fairly and support people through conflict or uncertainty.
tasks.altitude: The manager gains some preparation time for coaching and staffing discussions. Hiring, evaluation and delegation rights remain unchanged; this is administrative relief around a predominantly human task.

reach.task: Prepare cross-channel cover and development assignments.
reach.learn: Channel skill requirements, realistic learning time and fair workload allocation.

evidence.claim: Forms, enrolments, permissioned records and reminders are established personnel-system capabilities.
AI used for recruitment or employee evaluation can fall within the EU AI Act's high-risk employment categories.
The Netherlands has works-council consent provisions relevant to employee monitoring; national rules elsewhere vary.
Automating factual preparation does not establish that hiring, coaching or performance judgement should be automated.

assumptions: Steps describe activities across a management cycle; hiring occurs only when a vacancy exists.
Recruiters already provide shortlists; automated candidate ranking is outside this design.
Review packs contain agreed evidence, without inferred personality, productivity rankings or meeting surveillance.
Build ranges assume existing personnel systems; consultation and access may take longer under applicable national rules.
unknowns: Which hiring, training and evaluation approvals the manager holds.
Which personnel systems permit the required restricted views.
Which employee representatives must be consulted and on what timetable.
Which review records, retention periods and employee correction procedures apply.
research_questions: Can existing configuration produce useful evidence packs without creating a new personnel data store?
Can permissions prevent confidential review evidence from appearing in general delivery views?
Which administrative fields can be prefilled while keeping evaluation wording authored by the manager?
new_work: Check evidence packs for omissions and misleading context.
Maintain role permissions, retention settings and approval routes.
Handle enrolment failures and reminder exceptions.
Review employee corrections and keep consultation documentation current.
tasks.statement: Direct the hiring, training, or performance evaluations of marketing or sales staff and oversee their daily activities.

tasks.short: Negotiate distribution agreements with vendors or distributors.

steps.what: Review distribution volumes, service performance, costs and margins.
Request proposals from selected vendors or distributors.
Compare proposal prices, coverage, service commitments and commercial exceptions.

loop.input: Supplier proposals and a fixed commercial comparison schema.
loop.output: Source-linked proposal fields, exclusions and missing terms.
loop.check: Require page references; validate currencies, units and dates; calculate scenarios deterministically; reviewer checks material terms.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass per proposal; ambiguous terms go to procurement.
loop.why_not_simpler: Calculations are deterministic, but proposals describe coverage and exceptions in inconsistent free text.

steps.what: Agree negotiation limits, preferred coverage and acceptable commercial trade-offs.
Negotiate coverage, pricing, incentives and service commitments within the approved mandate.
Prepare the agreement using agreed terms and the approved contract template.
Review legal departures and approve the agreement for signature.
Sign the approved agreement and obtain the counterparty's signature.

tasks.design: Combine reporting from the {ERP} and {OPS_SYSTEM} with a proposal comparison generator that extracts source-linked terms and calculates scenarios deterministically. Populate approved templates in the {DOCS}, route legal and commercial approvals through the {WORKFLOW}, and release the approved version to the {ESIGN} after signatory approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Comparable costs require manual normalisation, while proposal exceptions sit in documents and email threads. Negotiation itself depends on bargaining power and trust.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding makes comparison tools and approval connections cheaper to build. Bounded extraction can structure proposals without giving software negotiating authority.
tasks.still_hard: Exclusivity, territorial rights, service risk and concessions need commercial and legal judgement. Missing operational data can make precise comparisons misleading.
tasks.human_edge: Read the counterparty's priorities, trade concessions and protect the long-term distribution relationship.
tasks.altitude: The manager spends less preparation time reconciling proposals and more time testing distribution options with operations and finance. Negotiation and signature limits stay unchanged.

reach.task: Assess market coverage gaps before distributor negotiations.
reach.learn: Territory analysis, channel overlap and evidence of unmet customer demand.

reach.task: Assess distributor promotion commitments against expected commercial value.
reach.learn: Incremental margin, promotion funding and measurable delivery commitments.

evidence.claim: Deterministic comparisons, template generation and signature routing can reduce preparation work while people retain negotiation and approval.
The supplied digest provides no documented case establishing automated distribution negotiation or its savings.
Time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured results.

assumptions: Negotiation produces provisional terms; binding acceptance follows the approval and signature process.
Approved contract templates and commercial approval limits exist.
Template departures are flagged for legal drafting rather than generated automatically.
Access timing includes confidentiality review and employee consultation under national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Whether marketing, procurement or a commercial director leads distribution negotiations.
Which proposal fields and contract templates are standardised.
Whether the {ERP} and {OPS_SYSTEM} support compatible supplier and service identifiers.
Which commitments negotiators can make before signature.
Which access and national consultation requirements apply.
research_questions: Can source-linked extraction reliably distinguish base prices from conditional rebates and exclusions?
Which scenario calculations remain comparable across differing service commitments?
new_work: Verify extracted material terms and resolve ambiguous proposal language.
Maintain comparison rules, contract templates and approval limits.
Check that the signed version matches the approved version.
Handle connector failures and incomplete operational records.
tasks.statement: Negotiate contracts with vendors or distributors to manage product distribution, establishing distribution networks or developing distribution strategies.

tasks.short: Agree product specifications with product development colleagues using customer, market and brand evidence.

steps.what: Collect customer feedback, market findings and current specifications.
Prepare a brief linking customer needs to specification choices.

loop.input: Selected consultation evidence, brand guidelines and a brief template.
loop.output: A specification brief with source references, options and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Check references resolve; the marketing manager verifies claims, relevance and omitted counterevidence.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per brief; missing evidence stays flagged for manual completion.
loop.why_not_simpler: Customer feedback is free text, and its implications cannot be filled from fixed fields alone.

steps.what: Discuss design, colour, packaging and feasibility trade-offs.
Approve specification changes within agreed product and budget authority.
Record agreed changes, reasons, owners and open questions.
Send the decision summary and follow-up responsibilities.

tasks.design: A small evidence collector assembles permitted records from the {CRM} and {DOCS}; a bounded drafting loop prepares a referenced specification brief. People discuss trade-offs and approve changes, capturing decisions in structured fields that generate the log in {DOCS}, follow-up tasks in {PROJECT} and notifications through {EMAIL}. Start with approved file imports where direct access is unavailable.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence was scattered, briefs required contextual reading, and decisions were recorded inconsistently. The discussion itself was never a straightforward automation target.
tasks.enabler_now: Document extraction, structured templates and ordinary integrations make preparation and recording easier to build. A bounded model can draft the narrative for review.
tasks.still_hard: Customer preferences conflict with manufacturing constraints. Physical samples, aesthetics and uncertain demand still require discussion and testing.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise weak evidence, negotiate trade-offs and judge how a physical product will feel to customers.

ambition.what: Run an evidence-backed packaging review at each prototype milestone.

tasks.altitude: The marketing manager spends less time assembling briefs and chasing decisions. They gain capacity to propose customer tests before specification approval; formal approval rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Design a customer comparison of two packaging options.
reach.learn: Sampling, neutral questions and the limits of preference evidence.

reach.task: Translate customer requirements into a packaging brief.
reach.learn: Print constraints, accessibility and how to specify visual requirements.

evidence.claim: Evidence collection, template drafting and structured decision records can support human product consultations; this specific design has no documented case in the digest.

assumptions: A typical mid-size company holds feedback in the {CRM} and specifications in {DOCS}.
Time shares are illustrative estimates, with conversation and approval taking most of the task.
The future workflow captures approved decisions in structured fields rather than inferring approval from a transcript.
Build ranges cover one product team and a small set of permitted sources.
unknowns: Where current specifications and customer evidence are actually held.
Who can approve specification changes and within what limits.
Whether exports or interfaces are available to the user.
Whether national rules require employee consultation for the proposed implementation.
research_questions: Does the brief preserve conflicting customer evidence as reliably as manual preparation?
Which structured decision fields prevent ambiguity without slowing the meeting?
new_work: Review generated briefs and check source references.
Resolve stale or contradictory product records.
Maintain evidence mappings, templates and access permissions.
Complete structured decision fields during approval.
tasks.statement: Consult with product development personnel on product specifications, such as design, color, or packaging.

tasks.short: Compile accurate, approved lists of products and services.

steps.what: Read product briefs and collect descriptions, benefits and service conditions.

loop.input: Product briefs, service conditions and approved claims.
loop.output: Draft offering facts with source passages and missing-field flags.
loop.check: Validate required fields and units; unsupported benefits remain blank for review.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair per brief; unresolved facts return to the product manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Narrative specifications vary in wording. Structured product fields bypass the loop.

steps.what: Export active product codes, approved prices and availability status.
Match descriptions to product codes and resolve duplicates or conflicting fields.
Choose which offerings and approved claims suit the audience.
Assemble and format the offering list using the approved template.
Check facts, claims and market scope, then approve the offering list.
Publish the approved offering list.

tasks.design: Configure offering records in the {WORKFLOW}, linked to authoritative product and price fields from the {ERP}. A bounded loop extracts draft facts from narrative briefs in the {DOCS}; deterministic matching and templates generate the list without inventing claims. The {CMS} publishes only the exact revision approved by the manager, with approval time counted in the preceding review step.
tasks.previous_blocker: Descriptions, prices and service conditions had different owners and update cycles. Manual matching and formatting concealed the absence of clear field ownership.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured records, existing imports and deterministic templates cover most work. AI-assisted coding reduces setup effort, and bounded extraction helps where source briefs remain narrative.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting product facts, unsupported claims and market-specific service conditions require accountable owners. Poor identifiers still cause matching exceptions.
tasks.human_edge: Select the right offer for the audience and recognise a technically accurate claim that could still mislead.

ambition.what: Approved offering lists for small partner sales teams previously relying on ad hoc descriptions.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time proofreading repeated facts and more time shaping audience-specific selections. They can define approved partner assortments within existing commercial limits; pricing authority does not change.

reach.task: Turn complex product capabilities and exclusions into clear customer descriptions.
reach.learn: Terminology control, source traceability and writing precise limitations.

reach.task: Maintain category attributes and validate published product information.
reach.learn: Product identifiers, attribute schemas and availability handling.

evidence.claim: HubSpot offers branded content drafting; this supports drafting capability, not verified product facts or automatic publication.
Identifier-based matching, required-field checks and template generation can be deterministic.
Public AI-generated material may require marking or disclosure under applicable AI Act Article 50 provisions.
Build ranges and remaining-time estimates assume a limited catalogue and usable identifiers.

assumptions: The first release covers one language, one market and one publication channel.
The {ERP} owns codes and prices; product owners own descriptions and conditions.
Matching uses explicit identifiers and configured aliases; ambiguous matches are held.
Publication approval is bound to the exact revision and invalidated by later changes.
Disclosure requirements are checked for the actual published material.
No employee monitoring is introduced; consultation under national rules is assessed if scope changes.
unknowns: Whether a current catalogue feature already supports the required records and templates.
How reliably product codes appear in narrative briefs.
Who owns each disputed field and claim.
Whether the {CMS} supports approval-bound scheduled publication.
Which access and national consultation procedures apply.
research_questions: Can existing catalogue configuration eliminate the separate matching workbook?
Which fields cause the most factual corrections after publication?
What proportion of source briefs already has structured fields and needs no model extraction?
new_work: Resolve unmatched codes and conflicting field values.
Maintain field ownership, templates and approved claims.
Review extracted facts and changed content.
Monitor stale records and failed publications.
Reapprove revisions when authoritative source facts change.
tasks.statement: Compile lists describing product or service offerings.

tasks.short: Forecast sales and profitability using business developments, market signals and explicit planning assumptions.

steps.what: Export sales, pipeline, costs and campaign results into a planning workbook.
Read market research, competitor developments and customer feedback.

loop.input: Dated market research, competitor observations and permitted customer feedback.
loop.output: Source-linked market signals, contradictions and evidence gaps.
loop.check: Require a source passage and date for each signal; separate observation from interpretation.
loop.stop: Process one selected source batch with one repair pass; unreadable or conflicting items go to review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Relevant developments occur in varied prose that keyword rules cannot reliably interpret.

steps.what: Reconcile periods, product groups and margin definitions with finance.
Build sales and margin scenarios with explicit demand, conversion and cost assumptions.
Challenge demand assumptions and commercial implications with sales and finance.
Approve the planning forecast and its material assumptions.
Publish the approved forecast pack and distribute its location.

tasks.design: Connect {CRM} and {ERP} to a governed forecast dataset in {DATA_PLATFORM}, with reconciliation rules and deterministic scenario calculations displayed in {BI}. A bounded extraction step turns selected research in {DOCS} into source-linked signals without changing forecast assumptions. Sales and finance challenge the scenarios, and only an approved forecast produces the published pack.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sales and finance used different definitions, and workbook adjustments were difficult to trace. Research interpretation was mixed into numerical forecasting.
tasks.enabler_now: Connectors, versioned assumptions and deterministic calculations are established technology. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of adapters and validation; bounded extraction reduces research preparation.
tasks.still_hard: Demand shocks, weak pipeline discipline and uncertain costs remain. A stage-weighted pipeline is a baseline, not proof of future revenue or marketing causality.
tasks.human_edge: Challenge optimistic assumptions, distinguish temporary noise from structural change and negotiate a credible shared forecast.
tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time rebuilding workbooks and more time testing commercial assumptions. Scenario exploration becomes more frequent; finance retains forecast approval and spending authority does not change.

reach.task: Design a targeted study to resolve a disputed demand assumption.
reach.learn: Sampling, response bias and how to express uncertainty.

evidence.claim: Connectors, standardised marketing data and automated reports are available today.
Pipeline probability and revenue forecast support exist; this does not establish local forecast accuracy.
Social listening and trend alerts can supply market signals.
Forecast quality must be checked on held-out historical periods and subsequent actuals.

assumptions: Historical sales, costs and dated pipeline snapshots can be obtained.
Finance provides margin definitions and approves material forecast assumptions.
Build ranges cover a limited set of product lines and share integration components with other tasks.
Access time includes data permissions and national employee consultation if the implementation changes employee monitoring.
unknowns: Whether historical pipeline snapshots exist.
Which forecast horizon, product hierarchy and margin definition are used.
Who signs off the planning forecast.
How much source data contains personal or confidential customer information.
research_questions: Which simple baseline performs best in historical backtesting at the required horizon?
How sensitive are margin scenarios to conversion, returns, cost allocation and sales timing?
Can source-linked extraction preserve contradictory evidence without overstating market signals?
new_work: Resolve reconciliation exceptions and maintain finance mappings.
Review extracted market signals and source permissions.
Version forecast assumptions and record overrides.
Compare forecasts with actuals and investigate systematic errors.
tasks.statement: Use sales forecasting or strategic planning to ensure the sale and profitability of products, lines, or services, analyzing business developments and monitoring market trends.

tasks.short: Choose products and accessories for trade shows.

steps.what: Agree the show's audience, commercial objective and display constraints.
Retrieve product specifications, launch dates and sample availability.
Compare candidates against space, transport, power and budget limits.
Inspect samples and assess appearance, demonstration quality and accessory fit.
Choose the display assortment with sales and product colleagues.
Prepare the approved item list, quantities, substitutes and handling notes.

tasks.design: Configure a product-selection view using catalogue and sample records from {ERP}, with venue constraints held in {WORKFLOW}. Deterministic checks flag infeasible combinations and generate a handover pack in {DOCS}; people inspect samples, choose the assortment and approve the pack before event preparation starts.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sample availability, product dimensions and event constraints sit in separate records. Physical display quality is poorly represented by catalogue fields.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured record views and small constraint-checking tools can join existing information cheaply. Template generation removes repeated preparation of item lists.
tasks.still_hard: Sample condition, live demonstrations and last-minute availability still need physical checks. Data upkeep may outweigh savings for very infrequent events.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing which combination tells a persuasive story and works well in a real exhibition space.
tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time checking dimensions and preparing handovers. More of the event preparation week goes to demonstrations and audience fit; selection and spending rights do not change.

reach.task: Translate a display selection into workable event logistics.
reach.learn: Venue constraints, transport lead times, accessibility and demonstration dependencies.

reach.task: Arrange products into a coherent visual display.
reach.learn: Sightlines, visual hierarchy and product grouping.

evidence.claim: Structured catalogue filtering, constraint checks and template generation are established deterministic patterns; the digest gives no direct assortment-selection case.
Physical sample assessment and commercial assortment selection remain human judgement in this design.

assumptions: Product and event constraints can be recorded as structured fields.
Shipment booking and purchasing are downstream tasks, outside this selection task.
Time shares and build ranges are estimates for a mid-size company.
Access review includes GDPR where contact data is used and any consultation required under national rules.
unknowns: Quality of product dimensions, weights and sample inventory.
Whether existing software already supports the required selection view.
Who approves product substitutions and event expenditure.
Event frequency and likely reuse of the tool.
research_questions: Which previous display failures could a structured constraint check have caught?
Would configuring an existing records view cost less than maintaining a separate tool?
new_work: Maintain sample status and venue constraint fields.
Review flagged combinations and missing specifications.
Check generated handover packs before release.
Record substitutions when samples become unavailable.
tasks.statement: Select products or accessories to be displayed at trade or special production shows.

tasks.short: Work with legal counsel to resolve copyright, licensing and royalty disputes.

steps.what: Collect disputed assets, rights agreements, correspondence and payment evidence.

loop.input: Documents from an explicitly selected case folder and permitted record exports.
loop.output: Evidence index identifying asset versions, parties, dates and missing documents.
loop.check: Retain originals and source references; verify dates and identifiers; manager checks completeness.
loop.stop: One classification pass and one correction pass; inaccessible or ambiguous items enter a missing-evidence list.
loop.why_not_simpler: Folder rules collect files, but inconsistent correspondence and asset descriptions need limited text interpretation.

steps.what: Prepare the chronology, business impact and questions for legal counsel.

loop.input: Evidence index, selected source passages and business impact notes.
loop.output: Factual chronology, disputed points and questions for counsel.
loop.check: Every factual assertion needs a source; distinguish allegations from established facts; manager checks omissions.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; unsupported statements remain explicit gaps.
loop.why_not_simpler: A fixed form captures fields, but a readable chronology requires synthesis across free-text sources.

steps.what: Assess rights, contractual obligations and legal response options.
Discuss legal options, commercial consequences and a preferred resolution.
Approve the remedy, settlement limits or escalation route.
Communicate the approved legal position to the producer or distributor.
Record resolution actions, responsible owners and deadlines.

tasks.design: Build a restricted evidence index from selected material in the {DOCS}, {EMAIL} and {ERP}; bounded loops draft a source-linked chronology and questions for counsel. Legal assessment and external responses stay with people, while the {WORKFLOW} creates actions in the {PROJECT} from structured, approved remedy fields.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence is scattered across asset versions, agreements and correspondence. Generic search retrieves documents but does not reliably establish a complete chronology.
tasks.enabler_now: Document indexing, source-linked extraction and template-based drafting can now be assembled with less coding effort. These support factual preparation without assuming improved legal reasoning.
tasks.still_hard: Rights ownership, territorial scope, disputed facts and settlement consequences require counsel. Confidentiality, privilege and access restrictions can make integration expensive.

Prepare the promotional pack from product facts and brand guidance.

tasks.statement: Integrate environmental information into product or company marketing strategies, policies, or activities.

tasks.short: Recommend product and packaging changes using environmental evidence, commercial constraints and specialist advice.

steps.what: Request material, packaging, production and supplier evidence.
Read evidence and extract material quantities, methods, dates and limitations.

loop.input: Supplier documents and internal evidence for the selected product.
loop.output: An evidence register with values, units, scope, dates, source passages and gaps.
loop.check: Validate units and required fields; a sustainability specialist checks consequential values and comparability.
loop.stop: Two extraction attempts per document; unreadable files and inconsistent evidence go to manual review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Supplier documents vary in wording and layout; fixed fields alone cannot recover scope and caveats.

steps.what: Compare feasible changes using common boundaries, costs and environmental measures.
Draft a recommendation explaining benefits, uncertainty, costs and customer implications.

loop.input: Reviewed option comparison, customer feedback and recommendation template.
loop.output: A referenced recommendation separating measured benefits, assumptions and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Every environmental assertion must match reviewed evidence; the marketing manager checks commercial interpretation.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unsupported benefits remain explicit evidence gaps.
loop.why_not_simpler: The recommendation combines contextual customer evidence with technical caveats that a fixed template cannot explain.

steps.what: Discuss feasibility, customer acceptance and environmental trade-offs with technical colleagues.
Approve a pilot or request stronger evidence.
Record the decision, evidence gaps and pilot responsibilities.

tasks.design: A configured request flow in {WORKFLOW} collects approved evidence into {DOCS}, and a bounded extraction loop builds a referenced register. Deterministic calculations compare only specialist-approved, comparable inputs; a second bounded loop drafts the recommendation. People select the pilot, and the approved decision creates responsibilities in {PROJECT}; public environmental claims require a separate publication approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supplier evidence was inconsistent, comparison boundaries differed, and specialist review was difficult to encode. Drafting recommendations added work without resolving those underlying evidence gaps.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded extraction and drafting can reduce document handling. Reusable calculation templates make assumptions and missing inputs visible.
tasks.still_hard: Reliable lifecycle evidence, burden shifting, supplier verification and customer acceptance remain expensive. Faster drafting does not establish environmental soundness.
tasks.human_edge: Question the comparison boundary, distinguish evidence from claims and balance environmental benefits against practical consequences.

ambition.what: Offer an evidence-backed packaging improvement shortlist for product renewal reviews.

tasks.altitude: The marketing manager brings clearer options and evidence gaps to product discussions. They can propose targeted pilots sooner, while technical validation and investment authority stay with the relevant specialists and approvers.

reach.task: Screen packaging alternatives before commissioning detailed assessment.
reach.learn: Functional units, lifecycle boundaries, uncertainty and evidence quality.

reach.task: Document the evidence supporting a proposed environmental benefit.
reach.learn: Traceable assertions, qualification language and document version control.

evidence.claim: Document extraction and deterministic comparison can support sustainability recommendations, but the digest supplies no product or case validating this application.
Environmental comparisons require compatible boundaries and expert interpretation; extraction alone cannot establish a product's environmental benefit.

assumptions: The marketing manager coordinates recommendations with technical and sustainability colleagues.
Calculations use approved methods and factors; the model does not invent environmental measures.
Time shares retain substantial human evaluation despite opportunities to accelerate drafting.
Build ranges cover a limited product category and exclude commissioning new lifecycle studies.
Access work includes supplier confidentiality and GDPR review where evidence contains personal data.
unknowns: Which supplier evidence is available and licensed for reuse.
Whether an internal or external sustainability specialist can validate comparisons.
Which environmental methods and decision thresholds the company accepts.
Who approves pilots and public environmental claims.
Whether national rules require employee consultation for the proposed implementation.
research_questions: Which document types produce reliable extraction of units, boundaries and exclusions?
Which comparison methods suit the selected product category?
What evidence is needed to substantiate the proposed public environmental claims?
new_work: Validate extracted technical values and source passages.
Resolve incompatible comparison boundaries and missing supplier evidence.
Maintain calculation methods, factors and their versions.
Review recommendation drafts and separate pilot hypotheses from publishable claims.
tasks.statement: Recommend modifications to products, packaging, production processes, or other characteristics to improve the environmental soundness or sustainability of products.

tasks.short: Coordinate marketing activities, budgets and delivery with advertising and promotion managers.

steps.what: Review objectives, campaign results and available budget.
Draft activities, audiences, messages and measures in a marketing plan.

loop.input: Planning baseline, brand guidelines, approved product claims and a fixed plan template.
loop.output: Draft marketing plan with source references and unresolved choices.
loop.check: Validate required fields, trace numbers and claims, and flag unsupported audience assumptions.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass; unresolved sections remain blank for the marketing manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates fill facts, but proposed messages and activity rationales need contextual writing.

steps.what: Agree channel priorities, delivery capacity and responsibilities with promotion managers.
Approve spending commitments and material policy changes.
Create campaign briefs, assign owners and set delivery dates.
Chase owners for progress and consolidate replies.
Review delivery and results, then decide corrective actions.

tasks.design: Configure a shared planning view in {BI} from {ERP}, {PROJECT}, {ADS} and {MARKETING_AUTOMATION}, with a bounded drafting step producing a marketing plan in {DOCS}. Approved plan fields create briefs and assignments in {PROJECT}; owners update delivery there, removing routine status chasing. People approve spending, policy changes and campaign adjustments, while external launch approval remains with the responsible promotion manager.
tasks.previous_blocker: Campaign identifiers, financial periods and ownership differed across systems. Writing and coordination were bundled together, making the whole task appear manual.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing connectors and configurable workflows cover much of the coordination. AI-assisted coding makes small mappings and template generators cheaper to build; a bounded model can draft the narrative.
tasks.still_hard: Channel attribution remains uncertain. Conflicting priorities, agency capacity and persuasive messages need human judgement; audience permissions and direct-marketing objections must be respected.
tasks.human_edge: Negotiate priorities, understand brand risk and secure commitments from people with competing demands.

ambition.what: Weekly campaign stop, repair or continue decisions.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from collecting updates to resolving delivery constraints and reviewing campaign choices. The manager can make more timely adjustments within existing authority; no additional spending rights are assumed.

reach.task: Prepare a coordinated channel launch calendar.
reach.learn: Channel lead times, creative dependencies and launch approval requirements.

evidence.claim: Marketing connectors and standardised reporting are available building blocks; local mappings still need validation.
Campaign planning and branded drafting capabilities exist, supporting the bounded drafting component.
Direct-marketing objections must stop the affected marketing, including associated profiling.
Removing duplicate status collection requires owners to maintain one shared delivery record.

assumptions: Owners can update delivery status in {PROJECT}; otherwise status chasing only shrinks.
Campaign launch and audience selection are separate controlled actions.
Build ranges estimate one reusable first release using existing licences and approved read access.
Consent and access time includes national employee-consultation requirements where applicable; waiting periods may exceed the estimate.
unknowns: Which source systems and connectors are available.
Who may approve spend, campaign adjustments and external launches.
Whether campaign identifiers and audience permission records are consistent.
Which national employee-consultation requirements apply.
research_questions: Can available connectors preserve campaign identifiers, reporting periods and source lineage?
Does the plan template produce useful briefs without unsupported audience or product claims?
new_work: Review drafted plans and unsupported claims.
Maintain campaign mappings, templates and approval limits.
Handle stale delivery records and failed data feeds.
Check audience permission controls before external activation.
tasks.statement: Formulate, direct, or coordinate marketing activities or policies to promote products or services, working with advertising or promotion managers.

GDPR, marketing permissions and applicable national employee-consultation rules.
